I don't know, I'm pretty sure some of the features that Google quietly adds to its products and services have saved me more times than I can remember. From things like unsending e-mails to real-time collaboration and cloud storage for telecommuting to fully fledged MS Office alternatives and photo storage, organization, and editing tools. I couldn't even do my job without half the stuff that google offers.

There's no arguing against the fact that they provide top notch products, but at what cost of personal privacy? It also causes an issue when a single entity holds that much power not only over your information, but over the ability for your business to function.

What would happen if Google suddenly decided to freeze your account(s), like PayPal has done with innumerable small businesses? How would it affect you and what recourse would you have? This may or may not be an immediate threat, but it is surely something to consider.

Of course it's something to consider. This is true of any and all companies, products, and software that we use as a business. What if Microsoft decides that the cloud is the future and stops supporting MS Office products as they currently exist? We'd be SOL there too. What if our Chinese manufacturer gets shut down or goes out of business or suddenly shoots up in price because they have to pay off some corrupt official? We have to find a new manufacturer that can handle the same products. What if our bank gets bought out and the new company changes our account policy so that we can't get payroll loans or credit for expansion plans?

There are contingency plans at most companies for things like this, including backups, record keeping and organization, and stock buffers. If something in the whole production process fails, we fix it.

Online privacy will always be an issue. No government or company is going to agree to completely ignore online content because it infringes on privacy. There are far too many security issues for that to be practical, even. And while I would agree that there are bad people out there who are willing to take advantage of access to information, that's true offline as well. People will be people, online or off, which means that regardless of whether or not your privacy is "protected" online, people who aim to do mischief will find a way.

I'm not saying that people who want to use other services and encryption methods are crazy, they're welcome to do so and I hope it accomplishes what they want! But I also think that most people have no problem with online privacy and would rather take advantage of the kinds of services that companies like google offer, and they should be able to do that, too.
